commits.message:
feat(taxonomy): permanent noise filter + automated daily candidate triage

Cost investigation via Langfuse: organic daily LLM spend before this
session was $0.00-0.85/day (avg ~$0.08/day). Aug 31 and Sep 1 spiked to
$6.78 and $2.92 -- 82% of the entire month's spend in two days -- but
that was a one-time manual backlog catch-up (family auto-classification
across 700+ job titles, description backfills, a 3,884-item candidate
triage), not organic email volume. The forward-looking risk is real
though: new candidates arrive daily and the queue was never being
cleared, so it would only ever grow. Two permanent fixes, both aimed at
making future review-queue growth self-limiting without recurring
manual sessions like today's:

1. Deterministic noise pre-filter (app/understanding/taxonomy/
   candidates.py): _is_noise_skill_term/_is_noise_job_title reject
   sentence fragments, verb-phrase starts ("Drive business alignment"),
   emails, unbalanced parens, spreadsheet table rows ("22 VD DATA
   ANALYST 4+Y ONSITE"), and person names (a small common-names list
   catches "Durga Prasad"/"Venkat Ram"-shaped two-word terms) BEFORE a
   term is ever queued as a candidate -- not as a later cleanup pass.
   Same shape-based rules validated today against a real 3,884-item
   backlog, where they caught 41% of it with zero LLM cost and clean
   precision on manual sampling. Wired into _candidate_terms (skills)
   and find_unknown_job_title (titles). This is the actual "fix it
   permanently" piece: junk now never reaches a human OR an LLM,
   for free, forever.

2. Automated daily LLM batch triage (scripts/hermes-900-daily-taxonomy-
   triage.py, scheduled via a host-level systemd service+timer -- same
   pattern and location as the existing hermes-graph-renew.service/
   .timer, which are also host config, not repo-tracked): whatever
   survives the deterministic filter each day -- genuinely ambiguous,
   plausible-looking terms -- gets a real judgment call via the LLM,
   batched ~40 terms per call (not one call per term; today's full
   backlog of ~2,300 ambiguous items took only ~60 calls total). Same
   systemd oneshot-service-plus-timer shape already used for
   hermes-graph-renew (docker exec hermes-api python scripts/...,
   OnFailure alerting), runs once daily. Capped at
   HERMES_TAXONOMY_TRIAGE_MAX_PER_RUN (default 500) per run, oldest
   candidates first, so a queue spike can't produce an unbounded LLM
   bill in one run. A batch whose LLM response fails to parse (after 3
   retries) is left pending for the next run or a human -- never
   silently auto-approved or auto-rejected on an LLM hiccup. Verified
   end-to-end against production: cleared the real remaining backlog
   (204 skills, 69 titles) down to 41 skills / 40 titles genuinely left
   for human review, using the already-configured anthropic/claude-
   haiku-4-5 (no model swap needed -- Haiku was already the cheapest
   suitable model on the gateway; the cost problem was call volume and
   frequency, not model choice).

New coverage in scripts/hermes-900-spam-taxonomy-check.py: sentence
fragments, verb phrases, an email, and a person's name are never
queued as skill candidates; a person's name, a table row, and a verb-
phrase sentence are never queued as job title candidates; a genuine
new term still survives both filters. Full regression suite run
against a fresh schema and freshly built image (each run needs a truly
fresh Postgres -- confirmed a stray failure on a second run without
resetting was test-state pollution from reusing the same database, not
a real regression): hermes-900-spam-taxonomy-check.py passes all 73
checks including the 2 new ones; every other failure in the suite
reproduces identically against the current, unmodified production
image in the same throwaway harness (missing live server, missing
Langfuse/MS Graph credentials) -- confirmed pre-existing environment
gaps, not regressions from this change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
